hypothesis: For a focused local browser receiver, one Computer Use key action for each of a, Space and Left generates an ordered trusted keydown/keyup pair in the receiver and leaves its application-maintained held-key set empty.
method: Open the self-contained local HTML fixture in the preinstalled Brave browser. Focus the receiver via its accessible button, then send exactly one separate sky.press_key action for a, space and Left, refreshing state after each. Preserve the visible DOM event log. Separately run the fixture-contract tests in a pinned WSLc Python image.
decision_rule: PASS only if each of the three actions yields exactly one trusted keydown then one trusted keyup for the expected code, the receiver remains the active element, and its held-key set returns to [] after every action. Otherwise preserve FAIL/STOP without retrying the key sequence.

environment.windows_app: preinstalled Brave selected from sky.list_apps; exact version unrecorded

scope_limits: Tests Windows browser DOM delivery and its internal pressed-key bookkeeping only.
This is not a hardware keyboard sensor and does not prove key state outside the browser/OS input path.
No X11, Doom, model call, game-time progression, threat, recovery, task effect or MAP01 completion is involved.
No live allocation is used or retried.
retry_policy: No repeated action after any uncertain result; observe once and retain the first outcome.
